register.name: Treasury bonds in the international market (Eurobond)
register.detail: Ministerio de Finanzas Públicas · Issued July 2025 · US$800M at 11 years, coupon 6.25% · US$700M at 30 years, coupon 6.875%
register.note: The IMF records a US$1.5 billion Eurobond issued in July 2025; the tranches, coupons and uses are as reported by Estrategia & Negocios
register.text: Guatemala issued US$1.5 billion of Treasury bonds in the international market in July 2025, in two tranches of 11 and 30 years. The Ministry of Public Finance said the proceeds would go to public investment, roads, the cash-transfer programme for older people and technical studies for the first Metro line, among other uses. It is the sovereign’s own borrowing in the international market.

register.name: Civil Aviation Recovery Program
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Approved 8 September 2026 · P508751 · investment project
register.note: Works at La Aurora, Mundo Maya and the airfields of Puerto Barrios, Quetzaltenango and Huehuetenango
register.text: A World Bank loan of US$250 million to strengthen the institutions, technical capacity and finances of Guatemala’s civil aviation sector, repair runways and aprons, rehabilitate control towers and train air traffic controllers and rescue and firefighting staff. The World Bank notes that tourism supports more than 500,000 jobs in Guatemala; the project serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Disaster risk management development policy loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO)
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Approved 25 September 2025 · P505784 · third operation of its kind · three-year drawdown period, renewable up to four times
register.note: Lets the government draw funds quickly after hurricanes, earthquakes or volcanic eruptions
register.text: A US$430 million World Bank development policy loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, which the government can draw quickly after a disaster. It supports policies that build resilience into agriculture, transport and housing, and widen social protection for households that suddenly lose income. It serves the food, shelter and livelihood standards when disaster strikes.

register.name: Smart Public Finance: data-driven public expenditure management
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Approved 16 September 2025 · investment project · first phase of a US$140M Central America programme
register.note: Guatemala is the first phase of a multiphase programmatic approach for Central America
register.text: A US$50 million World Bank investment project to plan and execute the public budget more efficiently, for education, health, social protection and basic infrastructure, to modernise the public finance systems, including protection against cyberattacks, and to improve coordination and data-driven decisions. It serves the seven standards through better use of the budget that finances them.

register.name: Rural Infrastructure and Mobility for Good Living Program
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · P178573 · appraisal document of 10 June 2025 · investment project · closing 31 December 2032
register.note: US$384 million for rural, departmental and national roads; about 450,000 people in the area of direct influence
register.text: A World Bank loan of US$400 million, carried out by the Ministry of Communications, Infrastructure and Housing, to improve climate-resilient road connectivity in lagging rural areas and the management of the national road sector. It gives priority to roads that improve local access, for instance to schools and health centres, which serves the education, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: CA-9 North Corridor Development Program: Teculután to Mayuelas
register.note: To raise the service level of the corridor and improve flood resilience in its area of influence
register.text: An IDB loan of US$350 million to improve the Teculután to Mayuelas section of the CA-9 corridor to the Atlantic, linking Guatemala’s international trade nodes, with a focus on road safety and climate resilience. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Rural Electrification Access Program (PAER)
register.detail: IDB · Approved 30 April 2025 · GU-L1192 · loan 5991/OC-GU · 25 years · 5.5-year grace · SOFR-based rate
register.note: About 70,000 households to gain access to electricity, in the municipalities with the lowest coverage
register.text: An IDB loan of US$250 million to extend and upgrade rural distribution networks, build renewable mini-grids with storage and install individual solar systems, with support for the National Electrification Institute (INDE). About 70,000 households are to gain electricity for the first time; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Program to Support the Expansion of Secondary Education
register.detail: IDB · Approved 15 February 2023 · GU-L1184 · five-year disbursement · 6.6-year grace · SOFR-based rate
register.note: About 231,000 students aged 12 to 20, mainly in rural and peri-urban areas
register.text: An IDB loan of US$100 million to build 500 new classrooms, renovate 3,300 schools, install solar power where schools lack electricity, provide about 1.4 million learning resources and train about 7,600 teachers, with resources for bilingual intercultural education. It serves the education standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Fundea: expanding financial inclusion for resilience and productivity in rural Guatemala
register.detail: IDB · Approved 24 September 2026 · GU-L1201, US$16M · GU-L1205, US$4M · in implementation
register.note: Two operations of US$16 million and US$4 million, US$20 million together
register.text: Two IDB operations approved on 24 September 2026, of US$16 million and US$4 million, with Fundea, to expand financial inclusion for resilience and productivity in rural Guatemala. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Campus San Cristóbal, education and sports complex
register.detail: CABEI · IDB Invest · C2F · syndicated financing · about 60% physical and financial progress, 17 June 2026
register.text: Syndicated financing of US$37.2 million from CABEI, IDB Invest and the Canadian fund C2F for Campus San Cristóbal in Mixco: a school from pre-primary to secondary level, a university complex and an Olympic-level sports campus, with scholarships for federated athletes. It is to widen learning opportunities for more than 11,000 students; it serves the education standard.

register.name: Financing for MSMEs, women entrepreneurs and sustainable lending, Banco Industrial
register.detail: IDB Invest · Announced 12 March 2026 · with blended finance from UK SIP and the CIF and a B loan from BlueOrchard
register.note: MSMEs are 98% of firms in Guatemala and generate 77% of employment
register.text: An IDB Invest loan of US$133 million to Banco Industrial to expand credit to micro, small and medium enterprises and to grow its loans to women entrepreneurs and its sustainable portfolio, with technical advice on environmental risk management. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Credit line for productive finance, employment and housing, Banco Promerica
register.detail: CABEI · Approved 17 November 2025 · credit line · MSMEs, women-led firms, social and middle-income housing
register.note: 264 companies to benefit; up to 19,300 jobs estimated
register.text: A CABEI credit line of US$100 million to Banco Promerica in Guatemala for investment and working capital of micro, small and medium enterprises, with priority for renewable energy, agriculture and climate adaptation and for firms led by women, and for loans to buy, build or improve social and middle-income homes. It serves the livelihood and shelter standards.

register.name: Green, housing and SME financing, Banco Industrial
register.detail: IFC · JICA · FinDev Canada · 22 September 2025 · US$190M from IFC · US$150M from JICA · US$75M from FinDev Canada
register.text: A financing package of US$415 million for Banco Industrial, structured and led by IFC with JICA and FinDev Canada, for green buildings and climate-smart agriculture, sustainable housing to reduce the housing deficit, and small and medium enterprises, particularly those led by women. It serves the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: MIPYMES Verdes II: green finance for small firms
register.detail: CABEI · KfW · European Union · concluded, announced 7 May 2026 · loans and partial credit guarantees through four partner financial institutions
register.note: More than US$3.3 million of loans and US$2.1 million of guarantees; phases I and II together placed more than US$14 million of loans
register.text: The second phase of a CABEI initiative, supported by the European Union and Germany through KfW, that mobilised more than US$5.4 million of loans and partial credit guarantees for micro, small and medium enterprises in Guatemala, all of the loans for renewable energy, energy efficiency and cleaner production. It generated nearly 200 jobs; it serves the energy and livelihood standards.

items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 31% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A cobbled street of pastel colonial houses under jacaranda trees in bloom, with people far off and mountains in the haze, Guatemala

items.name: AMUVE (Asociación de Mujeres Campesinas Mundo Verde)
items.text: An association of rural and Indigenous women in Loma Linda, El Palmar, Quetzaltenango, legally constituted in 2003, that grows and roasts high-quality organic coffee, about 35 quintales a year; nine of its ten members earn an income from their work in it, and a modern thresher and a business plan from the Dedicated Grant Mechanism for Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities widened its sales.

items.name: AGRIDESEM (Asociación de Mujeres Agrícolas para el Desarrollo de San Sebastián)
items.text: A women’s farming association in Champerico, Retalhuleu, that grows plantains on one hectare, about 2,500 plants, and sells them under its own registered brand, Doña Platanita, while it conserves and restores 20 hectares of mangrove forest on which its farming depends.

items.name: Fundea
items.text: An organisation that expands financial inclusion in rural Guatemala, with which the IDB approved two operations on 24 September 2026, of US$16 million and US$4 million, for financial inclusion for resilience and productivity in rural areas.
